title: JitFilt: Mitigate Jitter-based Side Channel Analysis Attacks
problem: Signal jitter emanating from cryptographic circuits can be exploited via jitter-based side-channel analysis (JitSCA) attacks using time-to-digital converters to conduct remote attacks.
motivation: Cryptographic circuits face critical vulnerability from jitter-based attacks; effective countermeasures are needed.
method: Signal jitter filter implementation using FPGA mixed-mode clock managers (MMCMs), phase-locked loops (PLLs), and IDELAY components to reduce signal jitter in cryptographic designs.
key_novelty: First countermeasure specifically designed to mitigate jitter-based side-channel analysis attacks on cryptographic hardware.
contributions: 166x protection improvement (5 million traces vs 30k for unprotected AES)
Full secret key protection up to 5 million traces
PLL-based filter shows highest JitSCA protection
limitations: Tested only on specific FPGA platform (Digilent ZedBoard); portability to other FPGA platforms unclear.
primary_theme: First countermeasure for jitter-based side-channel attacks
